title: Integral scalar localization preserves the specified exchange arrow
statement: For the canonical bounded constructible comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-comparisons] and a commutative square of separated finite-type k-schemes with characteristic different from ℓ, the source comparison followed by the specified continuous E exchange at scalar extension of K equals scalar extension of the specified integral exchange at K followed by the target comparison. No exchange or push comparison is inverted; properness and Cartesianity are not required.

proof.text: Prove abstractly that the push mate and the inverse pull conjugate have the same adjunct, using iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and mateEquiv_counit. Restrict the identity to the bounded constructible adjunctions using their actual counits.

Tensor balancing proves coherence of the underived pull comparisons. Exact scalar extension and inverse image derive it, and the derived composition constraints identify the pull-comparison cube. For arbitrary adjunctions the specified exchange has adjunct equal to the square comparison followed by the counit. The private proved mating and exchange lemmas give the formal combination; restriction and normalization for the specified concrete bounded functors remain.

theorem integralConstructible_exchange_equality
    (sq : CommSq g' f' f g) (K : integralConstructible ℓ E X) :
    integralConstructibleSourceHom ℓ E k f g K ≫
        (boundedConstructibleBaseChange (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) ℓ k sq).app
          ((integralScalarConstructible ℓ E X).obj K) =
      (integralScalarConstructible ℓ E Y').map
          ((boundedConstructibleBaseChange (integralCoeff ℓ E) ℓ k sq).app K) ≫
        integralConstructibleTargetHom ℓ E k f' g' K
